sections.heading: Fiji anchored to bottom of Nations Championship table after 11-try England rout
sections.body: Fiji remain 12th of 12 in the Nations Championship log following three consecutive defeats, carrying a tournament-worst points difference of -96. The scale of the struggle was highlighted by an 8-73 loss to England, a result the BBC described as a thrashing of a "sorry" Fijian side. Replacement Henry Pollock scored a second-half hat-trick as England crossed for 11 tries to end their own five-Test losing streak. Following a 17-33 defeat to Scotland in Round 3, Fiji face France next.

lead.why: Fiji's winless Nations Championship start and the defensive frailties exposed in the England rout remain the most significant story for the senior men's side.

sections.heading: Tevita Tuiloa launches Fiji Sevens collectable range to honour memorable moments
sections.body: Fiji Rugby and Coca-Cola Europacific Partners have launched a series of limited-edition cans and bottles featuring the men’s Sevens side. The collection celebrates eight specific highlights from the 2025 Hong Kong and Singapore tournaments. At a launch event in Suva, Commercial Director Tevita Tuiloa stated that "Fiji’s rugby story belongs to all of us" as the union looks to inspire young players. The Flying Fijians currently sit bottom of the Nations Championship table following their 17-33 loss to Scotland.

The result, which ended England's five-Test losing run, sits among the heaviest defeats behind Fiji's -96 points difference through three rounds. With Round four against France next up, it's the kind of tape nobody in the Fiji camp will want to be watching again.

With George Furbank currently occupying the England full-back role, Carpenter admits he is motivated by the direct competition. “It would be nice to have a very good performance against them and against that England competition,” Carpenter said.

sections.heading: England's Twickenham ticket demand trails South Africa and New Zealand sales
sections.body: England's Twickenham allocation for next month's Nations Championship finals weekend has lagged behind South Africa and New Zealand, who have both sold out their 1,000-strong overseas allocations, while England's home quota — upped from 1,500 to 2,000 after early demand — still had tickets on sale this week at £164.80. sections.heading: NBA Star Victor Wembanyama Completes Training Stint With Provence Rugby
sections.body: NBA superstar Victor Wembanyama has completed a training stint with French second-tier side Provence, citing the squad's camaraderie as a major inspiration. The 22-year-old Spurs forward participated in line-out drills, tackling practice, and conditioning sessions alongside the professional squad during his summer off-season. Wembanyama, who previously sought strength training with Shaolin monks, praised the club's environment, stating, "The training was really hard, really good for stability, movement patterns and developing strength, but I am more grateful for the experience."

sections.heading: France’s 1977 Grand Slam side remembered for its enduring impact
sections.body: The 1977 French side remains a benchmark for inspiration in international rugby, noted for a squad that commanded respect before a ball was even kicked. Featuring a legendary back row of Jean-Pierre Rives and Jean-Claude Skrela, the team’s Five Nations Grand Slam victory continues to define a specific era of French flair. Alongside iconic international outfits like the All Blacks, that 1977 cohort is frequently cited as a side that transcends mere statistics to capture the imagination of fans.

lead.why: This story contextualises the 1977 Grand Slam side's legacy within the broader history of inspiring teams.

sections.heading: Galthié fielded young France side without Dupont for All Blacks opener
sections.body: Back in July, Fabien Galthié took a youthful France squad to Christchurch for the Nations Championship's launch match, leaving out Antoine Dupont, Romain Ntamack, Thomas Ramos, Grégory Alldritt and Louis Bielle-Biarrey as the squad managed a heavy Top 14 workload. The clash doubled as Dave Rennie's first test in charge of the All Blacks, with every July and November fixture now counting toward the new competition's Finals qualification — a reminder of how far this young group has already come.

sections.heading: Italy's highest world ranking remains eighth, achieved in 2007 and 2024
sections.body: Italy's best-ever world ranking sits at eighth, a mark the Azzurri reached in 2007 and matched again in 2024. It remains the high-water mark for Italian rugby's global standing, and a measure of how far the current side still has to climb back after three straight losses this autumn, including a 10-57 defeat to Australia in Round 3. That run leaves Italy with a points difference of -94 heading into next month's meeting with reigning world champions South Africa.

sections.heading: Felipe Contepomi confirms Shaun Edwards and Mario Ledesma as assistants
sections.body: Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi has secured two major appointments to his backroom staff, with Shaun Edwards and Mario Ledesma signing on through to the 2027 Rugby World Cup. Edwards, who is currently working with the Red Roses, will join as defence coach, while former Pumas head coach Ledesma returns to lead the forwards. Contepomi noted, "Mario and Shaun arrive at Los Pumas with enormous international experience." The duo will begin their roles at the end of October.

sections.heading: Les Kiss backs Wallabies to return fire in Sydney rematch
sections.body: Wallabies head coach Les Kiss has urged his side to respond following a heavy 50-19 defeat to the All Blacks at Eden Park. The result marked Australia’s first loss under his tenure, snapping a five-match unbeaten run. Kiss remains confident in his squad's underlying culture despite the setback. "You get a knockback, you find out more about yourself and that’s what we’ll do," said Kiss, who is now prioritising technical adjustments in order to "turn the dial" for next Saturday's clash.

Harry Potter replaced him on the wing, with Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii shifting into midfield for the rest of the Test. sections.body: The Japan Sakura 7s secured the gold medal at the 20th Asian Games in Aichi, Nagoya, by defeating defending champions China 10-5 in a tight final. The victory marks a successful return to the top of the podium for the Japanese women, who last won the title two Games ago. Across the tournament, Japan showed consistency, maintaining their competitive edge throughout the final day to clinch the gold in a hard-fought contest against their closest regional rivals.

sections.body: The Japan Sakura 7s reclaimed the gold medal at the 20th Asian Games held in Aichi and Nagoya, defeating defending champions China 10-5 in a tightly contested final. The victory marks a significant achievement for the squad, who last secured the title two Games ago. While the Japan men’s team missed out on the final after a semifinal defeat to China, they successfully rebounded to claim the bronze medal by defeating Korea 17-5.

sections.heading: Japan Men's Sevens Stunned By China In Semifinal, Settle For Bronze
sections.body: Japan's men's Sevens side suffered a surprise exit at the Asian Games in Nagoya, beaten 10-7 by China in the semifinal on the tournament's final day — a result Rugby Asia 247 called one of the weekend's upsets. Hosts Japan regrouped to claim bronze with a 17-5 win over Korea, who left the Games without a medal for the first time. The women's Sakura Sevens took gold, beating China 10-5 in their final, rounding off a mixed weekend for Japan's sevens programme.

sections.heading: New Zealand thrash Australia 50-19 to retain the Bledisloe Cup

After a competitive first half, the All Blacks surged away to score five second-half tries, extending their unbeaten streak at the venue to 54 matches. Despite the win, Dave Rennie faces fresh injury concerns: Scott Barrett failed an HIA, Leroy Carter suffered an ankle injury after scoring, and Anton Segner departed with a head wound.
